chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the shade for the one in Ihram, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Brightness is for the One for whom you are wearing Ihram.' I said, 'I am feverish and the heat is intense upon me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you not know that the sun sets along with the sins of the ones in Ihram?'

key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in Ihram (state of ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of shade for a pilgrim in Ihram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the spiritual nature of the shade (*dhilal*) granted to a pilgrim in Ihram, identifying it as a divine gift from Allah for the sake of the pilgrim. When the narrator mentions his physical sensitivity to heat, the Imam offers a profound cosmological insight: the sun sets due to the sins of those in Ihram, suggesting that the state of Ihram itself invokes divine mercy to alleviate environmental hardships. This highlights the Shia understanding of the interplay between ritual purity, divine grace, and the natural world.
